todaysEvents.delta: Up: Iran's IRGC (Jul 11) declared the Strait of Hormuz closed after firing on Cyprus-flagged container ship GFS Galaxy; one crew member missing, 23 rescued by Oman. The IRGC warned any unauthorized transit will draw further fire.

Up: CNN/AP (Jul 11) report the US launched a third wave of strikes this week, hitting 140 Iranian military targets across southern Iran, including coastal defenses near Bushehr nuclear plant, in response to the container ship attack.

todaysEvents.summary: Regional war expands to five nations
todaysEvents.delta: Up: Al Jazeera/DW (Jul 12) report Iran struck US bases in Jordan (Prince Hassan Air Base), Qatar (Al Udeid, intercepted; 3 wounded), Kuwait (intercepted), and Oman (aircraft carrier refueling platforms). Qatar's Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani died during the attack.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A diplomatic off-ramp re-emerges as international pressure mounts amid the weekend escalation. Iran partially reopens the Strait in exchange for mediated talks, and the US halts further strikes. Brent settles $85-95/bbl as the risk premium partially deflates. Probability cut to 15% after Hormuz formal closure and multi-country conflict expansion.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Hormuz remains effectively closed with episodic openings for escorted vessels. US-Iran strikes continue at a constrained tempo while ad-hoc mediation continues. Brent trades $95-120/bbl, JKM surges toward $25-30/MMBtu, iTraxx Asia IG breaks 150bp. ASEAN importers face severe supply chain disruption.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Full Hormuz blockade endures. Iran seizes further vessels; US strikes escalate to strategic Iranian infrastructure. Regional conflict draws in more Gulf states. Brent spikes $115-140+/bbl with sustained outages; JKM above $35/MMBtu; Asian credit markets dislocate. Probability raised to 55% after formal Hormuz closure, 140-target US strikes, and multi-country retaliation.
